newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian gangsters killed in roadblock shoot-out.
newsitem.headline: Albanian gangsters killed in roadblock shoot-out.

text.p: Two gangsters were killed trying to shoot their way through a police roadblock in southern Albania during the night, the state news agency ATA reported on Tuesday.
Three other gangsters and two policemen were wounded in the gun battle, which lasted three hours, the agency said.
The five gangsters were travelling in a car without number plates, ATA said. When police stopped them at a roadblock in Erseke, 250 km (155 miles) south-east of the capital, Tirana, they opened fire.
Southern Albania has been plagued by armed gangs since the collapse of bogus investment schemes unleashed widespread chaos and lawlessness early this year.
An estimated one million weapons are still in private hands. Albanians have been given until September 30 to hand in arms looted from military barracks.
On Monday, six people wanted for rape, murder and robbery were killed by machine-gun fire from a rival gang as their car entered a village near Kucove.
Local newspapers also reported on Tuesday that a member of the ruling Socialist Party, who was close to Prime Minister Fatos Nano, had been shot dead while taking a walk with his family in Tirana.
